nodes.label: Pruritic and painful periorbital eruption lasting 1 month
Patient is a woman in her 70s

Medical history includes lupus nephritis requiring hemodialysis, immune thrombocytopenia, acute myeloid leukemia, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, deep vein thrombosis, diverticulitis, and postcolectomy diarrhea
Past treatments included hydroxychloroquine which resulted in retinal toxic effects, and lenalidomide which severely worsened platelet count with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL
Physical examination demonstrated scaly, crusted pink plaques involving the periorbital skin
Skin biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy
Pathologist notes that the patient's medication history was not obtained in the historical record
Periorbital eruption may be drug-induced interface dermatitis (drug-induced lichenoid reaction)
